reason: E2 directly supports the thermodynamic drive for B2 ordering in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni and its temperature dependence, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence for sluggish diffusion delaying ordering in this specific alloy or for the predicted kinetic control of B2 formation via cooling rate.
premises: Strong negative mixing enthalpies between Al–Ni and Al–Co drive B2 ordering
Sluggish diffusion in multicomponent alloys delays ordering kinetics
Slow cooling or annealing provides time to overcome kinetic barriers, enabling B2 formation
Rapid quenching suppresses ordering, retaining disordered BCC
Ordering leads to compositional partitioning into B2 (Al,Ni,Co-rich) and disordered BCC (Cr,Fe-rich)
